title: Reading Drill — Planning benches at a railway museum — Preparing a second trial
description: One short passage, six questions. Recommended time: 10 minutes.

passages.title: Planning benches at a railway museum — Preparing a second trial
passages.body:
**A** In Cairnford, work on visitors unable to rest near the longest information displays had already produced a small collection of short observation sessions. The gallery planner used this material to plan a second trial. The first report contained several different figures, but for the second trial the group agreed to publish one main outcome: seats occupied at busy times.

**B** The group kept a bench near the longest display for the new trial, which was planned to run for nine weeks. Volunteers were shown a sample record before starting. They were also asked to describe anything unusual in a separate note, so later readers could tell the difference between an ordinary value and one taken during a disruption.

**C** The trial design stated that temporary school tours should be recorded even when everything else appeared normal. If this information was missing, the team would leave the field blank rather than infer an answer. It would publish a provisional finding and label it clearly if too few readings were available for a reliable result.
